R127.note: Content-sniffed MIME mapped to a server-chosen extension plus a random filename removes the client name from the stored path entirely; the loss of the recognizable filename and the fileinfo dependency are both stated plainly and legitimate image uploads still succeed.

R128.note: strnlen(line, LINE_CAPACITY) rejection guarantees a terminator within the allocation before sscanf reads, and %255s correctly bounds the 256-byte destination; the only rejected inputs are unterminated lines the original could only parse via out-of-bounds reads, and the change is stated.

R129.note: Single-component check (no separators, not . or ..) appended to a realpath'd base makes containment structural for a not-yet-existing file; the switch to exclusive-create ('xb', 409 on existing name) is stated and matches the header's 'name a new file' contract.

R130.note: Switching {!! !!} to {{ }} routes the value through e() and nothing upstream produces HTML, so escaping is the right shape; the write-up states openly that it chose escaping over sanitization because the field carries plain text despite its descriptionHtml name.

R131.note: Host allowlist plus relative-reference branch is the right shape, but reproduced with JDK 26 in a scratch dir: new URI("///evil.example/x") yields host=null and rawAuthority=null so it passes the 'relative' branch, and Tomcat's sendRedirect treats a leading // as scheme-relative, producing http:///evil.example/x which browsers resolve to evil.example - the vector is only partially closed; the allowlist and 400 response are stated and legitimate same-site/example.org redirects still work.

R132.note: lockoutOnFailure: true restores Identity's AccessFailedAsync counting with default Lockout options; the added IsLockedOut message branch is stated and only affects accounts that are locked out.

R133.note: escapeshellarg() on both fallback operands, mirroring the primary path, closes shell-metacharacter injection while keeping the return values and discarded outputs per the contract; a leading-dash value could still be read as an option by legacy-convert, but that gap is unchanged from the original and outside the reported vector.

R134.note: Reproduced with Windows PowerShell 5.1 in a scratch dir: powershell.exe joins every argument after -Command into the script text rather than binding it to param(), so $ServerName is empty, a plain 'localhost' becomes a stray token that breaks Test-Connection for every legitimate call, and 'localhost; Set-Content ...' executed and wrote a marker file - the injection is not closed and the endpoint is silently broken.

R135.note: toRealPath() on both base and target with Path.startsWith closes traversal and symlink escape, but the up-front isAbsolute() rejection also refuses an absolute path that resolves inside BASE_DIR (e.g. /var/app-data/reports/x.txt), which the original read and the stated contract says should still be returned; the write-up states the check but not that it narrows the accepted set.

R136.note: bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) replaces the time-derived uniqid() with 128 bits of CSPRNG output; dropping the attacker-supplied client_nonce prefix and the resulting token-shape change are stated and no downstream consumer is affected.

R137.note: ODBC positional ? placeholder with the %...% wildcards moved into a typed OdbcParameter value removes all user data from the SQL text; result projection, exception propagation, and null-searchTerm behaviour ('%%') are unchanged.

R138.note: html/template contextual escaping at the render sink neutralizes Author and Excerpt with the same markup, header, and response path as the original fmt.Sprintf version, and no upstream file changes.
